parameters.content:
## Core Processor
Callable sub-workflow -- the single source of truth for turning one Graph 'message' object into a ticket (or a correctly-logged non-ticket outcome). Called by both Main (real-time) and Reconciliation (safety net). Never triggered directly.

Key guarantee: the lock loop below makes it safe for many concurrent invocations of THIS workflow -- from either caller -- to run at the same instant without racing each other on the Excel table.

## Lock loop (best-effort optimistic lock)
Excel has no atomic compare-and-swap, so this is write-then-verify-ownership, not a true distributed lock. Residual race window: the brief gap between our WRITE landing and our READ-back returning, during which another execution's WRITE could interleave. In practice this window is small (a network round trip) and the ownership check catches it when it happens -- the loser just retries with backoff. For a mathematically airtight guarantee you'd want a real lock primitive (Redis/Postgres advisory lock) -- out of scope for an Outlook+Excel-only stack, noted here as the upgrade path if ticket volume ever grows enough to matter.

## Critical section kept short
The lock is held only for: dedupe lookups, ticket-ID uniqueness loop, and the Excel append. The email reply and folder move happen AFTER release. This matters -- holding a global lock during a slow network send would serialize every concurrent ticket behind the slowest email send, which is exactly what we don't want under 'multiple emails per second' load.
